title: Legislative districts of Southern Leyte
wikitext:
{{Politics of the Philippines}} The '''legislative districts of Southern Leyte''' are the representations of the [[Provinces of the Philippines|province]] of [[Southern Leyte]] in the [[List of legislatures of the Philippines|various national legislatures]] of the [[Philippines]]. The province is currently represented in the [[House of Representatives of the Philippines|lower house]] of the [[Congress of the Philippines]] through its [[#1st District|first]] and [[#2nd District|second]] congressional districts. == History == {{further|Legislative districts of Leyte}} Prior to gaining separate representation, areas now under the jurisdiction of Southern Leyte were represented under the undivided province of [[Leyte (province)|Leyte]] ([[Legislative districts of Leyte#1907–1931 2|2nd]] and [[Legislative districts of Leyte#1907–1931 3|3rd]] districts, 1907–1931; [[Legislative districts of Leyte#1931–1961 3|3rd district]], 1931–1961). Republic Act No. 2227, enacted on May 22, 1959, created the province of [[Southern Leyte]] from the southern municipalities of Leyte that constituted its [[Legislative districts of Leyte#1931–1961 3|third congressional district]].{{cite web|title=Republic Act No. 2227 - An Act Creating the Province of Southern Leyte|url=http://www.lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra1959/ra_2227_1959.html|website=The LawPhil Project|access-date=August 1, 2019|date=May 22, 1959}} Per Section 5 of R.A. 2227, the incumbent representatives of all five districts of Leyte continued to serve for the remainder of [[4th Congress of the Philippines|4th Congress]]. Southern Leyte began to elect a separate representative under its own name starting in the [[1961 Philippine House of Representatives elections|1961 elections]]. Southern Leyte was represented in the [[Interim Batasang Pambansa]] as part of [[Interim Batasang Pambansa#Regional Representatives|Region VIII]] from 1978 to 1984. The province returned [[#At-Large (defunct)|one representative, elected at-large]], to the [[Regular Batasang Pambansa]] in [[1984 Philippine parliamentary election|1984]]. Under the new Constitution which was proclaimed on February 11, 1987, the province constituted a lone district{{cite web|title=1987 Constitution of the Philippines - Apportionment Ordinance|website=Official Gazette of the Republic of the Philippines|url=http://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/constitutions/the-1987-constitution-of-the-republic-of-the-philippines/the-1987-constitution-of-the-republic-of-the-philippines-ordinance/|author=1986 Constitutional Commission|date=February 2, 1987|access-date=November 19, 2017}} which elected its member to the restored [[House of Representatives of the Philippines|House of Representatives]] starting [[1987 Philippine legislative election|that same year]]. The signing of Republic Act No. 11198 on February 1, 2019{{cite web|url=https://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/downloads/2019/01jan/20190201-RA-11198-RRD.pdf|title=Republic Act No. 11198 - An Act Providing for the Reapportionment of the Province of Southern Leyte into Two (2) Legislative Districts|date=February 4, 2019|access-date=August 1, 2019|author=Congress of the Philippines}} reapportioned Southern Leyte into two legislative districts. Given that it was already too late for the [[COMELEC|Commission on Elections]] to change the old congressional district configuration data in the automated election system in time for the [[2019 Philippine House of Representatives elections|May 2019 polls]], COMELEC Resolution No. 10524 was promulgated to delay the elections for the two new districts to a date no less than six months from May 13, 2019.{{cite web|url=http://www.comelec.gov.ph/?r=2019NLE/Resolutions/res10524|title=IMPLEMENTING RULES AND REGULATIONS OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 11243 ENTITLED, "AN ACT REAPPORTIONING THE FIRST LEGISLATIVE DISTRICT OF THE PROVINCE OF SOUTH COTABATO, THEREBY CREATING THE LONE LEGISLATIVE DISTRICT OF GENERAL SANTOS CITY."|date=April 11, 2019|access-date=May 6, 2019|author=Commission on Elections}} By virtue of COMELEC Resolution No. 10552, the date of the elections for the [[#1st District|first]] and [[#2nd District|second]] districts of Southern Leyte was set for October 26, 2019.{{cite web|url=https://www.comelec.gov.ph/php-tpls-attachments/2019NLE/Resolutions/com_res_10552.pdf|title=COMELEC Resolution No. 10552 - IN THE MATTER OF: (1) SETTING THE DATE OF THE FIRST REGULAR ELECTIONS FOR MEMBER, HOUSE OF REPRESENTATIVES FOR THE FIRST AND SECOND LEGISLATIVE DISTRICTS OF SOUTHERN LEYTE, AND THE FIRST AND THIRD (LONE) LEGISLATIVE DISTRICTS OF SOUTH COTABATO; AND (2) PRESCRIBING THE CALENDAR OF ACTIVITIES AND PERIODS OF CERTAIN PROHIBITED ACTS IN CONNECTION WITH THE SAID ELECTIONS.|author=Commission on Elections|author-link=Commission on Elections (Philippines)|date=July 25, 2019|access-date=August 1, 2019}} On October 10, 2019, the COMELEC regional office for [[Eastern Visayas]] suspended the special elections and delayed it to November 30, pending the [[Supreme Court of the Philippines]] issuing a certificate of finality in a related case in which COMELEC was found to violate the law by setting separate special elections for the reconfigured [[Legislative districts of South Cotabato#1st District|1st Congressional District of South Cotabato]] and the newly created [[Legislative district of General Santos|Lone Congressional District of General Santos City]] instead of the next regular (i.e., 2022) election.{{cite web| website=Manila Bulletin |first=Marie Tonette |last=Marticio |url=https://news.mb.com.ph/2019/10/10/comelec-suspends-southern-leyte-special-poll-preps |title=COMELEC suspends Southern Leyte special poll preps |date=October 10, 2019 |access-date=March 14, 2020}}{{cite web|url=https://www.pna.gov.ph/articles/1084123 |title=Comelec suspends Oct. 26 congressional polls in Southern Leyte |first=Ferdinand |last=Patinio |date=October 24, 2019 |website=Philippine News Agency |access-date=March 14, 2020}} Ultimately, no special elections were carried out. Instead, on December 11, 2019, COMELEC — taking into account the September 10, 2019 Supreme Court ruling on the South Cotabato case (Vice Mayor Shirlyn L. Bañas-Nograles, et al. Vs. Commission on Elections{{cite web |url=http://sc.judiciary.gov.ph/6660/ |date=September 10, 2019 |access-date=March 14, 2020 |title=G.R. No. 246328 - Vice Mayor Shirlyn L. Bañas-Nograles, et al. Vs. Commission on Elections |website=[[Supreme Court of the Philippines]] |author=Supreme Court en Banc}}) — adopted the recommendation of its legal department to direct the Special Provincial Board of Canvassers for the Province of Southern Leyte to count the votes cast in the May 2019 elections.{{cite web| first=Jani |last=Arnaiz |title= Rep. Mercado proclaimed as Congressman for lone District of Southern Leyte |url=http://www.maasinreporter.com/southernleyte.php |website=The Reporter |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191225093827/http://www.maasinreporter.com/southernleyte.php |archive-date=December 25, 2019 |date= December 17, 2019 |access-date=March 14, 2020}} Roger Mercado was certified as the duly elected representative on December 16, 2019 by the Southern Leyte Provincial Board of Canvassers, and took his oath as the representative of the Lone Congressional District the next day.{{cite web| website=Manila Times |title=Southern Leyte lawmaker takes oath as newest House member |last=Tolentino |first=Reina C. |url=https://www.manilatimes.net/2019/12/17/news/latest-stories/southern-leyte-lawmaker-takes-oath-as-newest-house-member/665153/ |date=December 17, 2019 |access-date=March 14, 2020}} The [[#1st District|1st]] and [[#2nd District|2nd]] districts began electing their own representatives starting from the [[2022 Philippine House of Representatives elections|2022 elections]]. == Current districts == Southern Leyte's current congressional delegation is composed of two members. {{Color box|{{party color|National Unity Party (Philippines)}}|border=darkgray}} [[National Unity Party (Philippines)|NUP]] (1)
